items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I never liked Bix Beiderbecke. I never understood what the hollering was all about.

ctx.x: I have known Trumbauer what an excellent musician he was, and he really did, if you think about it --

Oh, yeah, I do believe it, yes. I do believe that. And I like Trumbauer myself. That's one of the few musicians from that circle -- I never liked Bix Beiderbecke. I never understood what the hollering was all about. And the funny thing, the first person that made me see any value at all, was Lloyd Reese, a black trumpet player. And he said, don't put him down just because he doesn't sound like Louis Armstrong. He said, there's a lot to learn from him. And he pointed it out but at that time I couldn't see it. Now,…

Yet, to take the opposite side of what you say of events, I agree with you on events, the young black player, perhaps, he might be crowded. But now that we have schools and quite a number of our young black musicians are in school, and we have jazz workshops, we have some people -- we're beginning to get into that. But I find that some of our regular -- some of our popular black stars are not -- don't go back and do a Louis Armstrong song in 1979. I happen to remember hearing some black instrumentalist that had…
